docs.title: TC-D86: Export Google Sheet as CSV
docs.text:
Prompt

"Export {SPREADSHEET_ID} as CSV"

Checks - Response encoding is utf-8 - content is comma-separated text matching the sheet's data

docs.title: TC-D87: Unknown export format
docs.text:
Prompt

"Export {DOC_ID} in format 'xyz'"

Checks - Returns a ValueError with a message listing valid formats - Not a server crash

docs.title: TC-D88: Upload plain text file ⚠️ requires-oauth
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload a plain text file called 'qa-upload.txt' to {FOLDER_ID} with content 'Hello from QA'"

Checks - File appears in {FOLDER_ID} with mimeType: text/plain - name is 'qa-upload.txt' - Folder cache invalidated — list_files shows the new file

docs.title: TC-D89: Upload Markdown as raw file (no conversion) ⚠️ requires-oauth
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload a markdown file called 'qa-notes.md' to {FOLDER_ID} with content '# Heading - item 1 - item 2' and do not convert it to a doc"

Checks - File created with mimeType: text/markdown (or text/plain — note whichever) - Markdown syntax is preserved as literal text — no conversion - convert_to_doc was False

docs.title: TC-D90: Upload Markdown and convert to Google Doc ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload this markdown to {FOLDER_ID} as a Google Doc called 'QA-Markdown-Doc': # My Title ## Section One - Bullet A - Bullet B Some **bold** text and a [link](https://example.com)."

Checks - A Google Doc is created (not a raw .md file) - Open in browser: 'My Title' renders as Heading 1 - 'Section One' renders as a heading - Bullet A and B render as a list - bold renders as bold text - 'link' is a hyperlink to https://example.com

docs.title: TC-D91: Upload HTML and convert to Google Doc ⚠️ requires-oauth
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload this HTML to {FOLDER_ID} as a Google Doc called 'QA-HTML-Doc': <h1>HTML Title</h1><p>A paragraph.</p><ul><li>X</li><li>Y</li></ul>"

Checks - Google Doc created with formatted content - Heading and list visible in browser - source_format was html, convert_to_doc was True

docs.title: TC-D92: Upload Markdown with table ⚠️ requires-oauth
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload this markdown as a Google Doc called 'QA-Table-Doc' to {FOLDER_ID}: # Table Test | Col A | Col B | |---|---| | 1 | 2 | | 3 | 4 |"

Checks - Google Doc created - Open in browser: a 2×2 table is visible under the heading - Confirms markdown[extra] extension handles GFM tables

docs.title: TC-D93: Upload a binary file ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload the local file /tmp/qa-test.png to {FOLDER_ID}" (create any small PNG at that path first)

Checks - File appears in Drive with mimeType: image/png - skipped: false in response - list_files for {FOLDER_ID} includes the new file after upload

docs.title: TC-D94: skip_if_exists prevents re-upload ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt (run twice, same file)

"Upload /tmp/qa-test.png to {FOLDER_ID} again"

Checks - Second call returns the existing file's fileId with skipped: true - No duplicate created in Drive - Confirms the pre-check list query fires and short-circuits

docs.title: TC-D95: skip_if_exists=False creates duplicate ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload /tmp/qa-test.png to {FOLDER_ID} with skip_if_exists set to false"

Checks - A second file with the same name is created in Drive - Response skipped: false - 🔍 Drive allows duplicate names — both files now exist

docs.title: TC-D96: Non-existent local path ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload the file /tmp/does-not-exist-qa.bin to {FOLDER_ID}"

Checks - ValueError raised with a message referencing the missing path - No Drive API call made

docs.title: TC-D97: Name override ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload /tmp/qa-test.png to {FOLDER_ID} but name it 'renamed-in-drive.png'"

Checks - File in Drive is named renamed-in-drive.png, not qa-test.png - Local file unchanged

docs.title: TC-D98: Bulk upload of a mixed directory ⚠️ destructive ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload all files from /tmp/qa-folder/ to {FOLDER_ID}" (create a directory with 2–3 files of different types)

Checks - All files appear in Drive with correct MIME types - uploaded list matches the filenames - failed is empty

docs.title: TC-D99: .DS_Store excluded by default ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Upload the directory /tmp/qa-folder/ to {FOLDER_ID}" (ensure .DS_Store exists in that directory)

Checks - .DS_Store is absent from the uploaded list and from Drive - Other files in the directory are uploaded normally

docs.title: TC-D100: skip_if_exists batches the existence check ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt (run twice)

"Upload /tmp/qa-folder/ to {FOLDER_ID} again with skip_if_exists=True"

Checks - Previously uploaded files appear in skipped - uploaded contains only new files (if any) - Only one list API call is made per run (not one per file) — check server logs

docs.title: TC-D101: Download a non-Google file ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download the file {BINARY_FILE_ID} to /tmp/qa-downloads/" (use the ID of the PNG uploaded in TC-D93)

Checks - File written to /tmp/qa-downloads/<drive_name> - size_bytes matches the Drive file size - File is a valid PNG (can be opened)

docs.title: TC-D102: Export Google Doc as plain text ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download {DOC_ID} as a txt file to /tmp/qa-downloads/"

Checks - File written as <doc_name>.txt - Content is readable plain text matching the doc body - encoding for the response is not relevant here — file is on disk

docs.title: TC-D103: Export Google Doc as PDF ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download {DOC_ID} as a pdf to /tmp/qa-downloads/"

Checks - File written as <doc_name>.pdf - File opens as a valid PDF (%PDF header) - size_bytes > 0

docs.title: TC-D104: Export Google Sheet as CSV ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download {SPREADSHEET_ID} as CSV to /tmp/qa-downloads/"

Checks - CSV file written locally - Content matches the spreadsheet's first sheet data

docs.title: TC-D105: Workspace file without export_format ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download {DOC_ID} to /tmp/qa-downloads/ without specifying a format"

Checks - ValueError raised mentioning that export_format is required - No file written

docs.title: TC-D106: local_path as exact file path ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download {BINARY_FILE_ID} and save it to /tmp/qa-specific-name.png"

Checks - File written to exactly /tmp/qa-specific-name.png, not into a subdirectory - Parent directory created if it didn't exist

docs.title: TC-D107: Download folder with mixed content ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download all files from {FOLDER_ID} to /tmp/qa-folder-download/"

Checks - All non-Workspace files written to the local directory - Workspace files (Docs, Sheets) listed in skipped — not exported without export_format - downloaded list matches non-Workspace filenames

docs.title: TC-D108: Download folder with export_format ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download all files from {FOLDER_ID} to /tmp/qa-folder-export/ with export_format='pdf'"

Checks - Non-Workspace files downloaded as-is - Workspace files exported as .pdf and included in downloaded - All resulting files have .pdf extension or original extension

docs.title: TC-D109: skip_if_exists=True skips existing local files ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt (run twice)

"Download {FOLDER_ID} to /tmp/qa-folder-download/ again"

Checks - Files already present locally appear in skipped - downloaded is empty (or contains only new Drive files)

docs.title: TC-D110: mime_type_filter ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Download only Google Docs from {FOLDER_ID} to /tmp/qa-docs-only/ using export_format='txt'"

Checks - Only application/vnd.google-apps.document files exported - Other file types absent from the output directory

docs.title: TC-D111: dry_run shows full action plan ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Do a dry run sync of {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ in bidirectional mode"

Checks - Response includes actions list with {name, action, reason} for every file - dry_run: true in response - No files created or modified locally or in Drive

docs.title: TC-D112: Bidirectional — Drive-only file downloaded ⚠️ destructive ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ bidirectionally" (ensure at least one file exists in Drive but not locally)

Checks - Drive-only files appear in downloaded - Files written to /tmp/qa-sync/

docs.title: TC-D113: Bidirectional — local-only file uploaded ⚠️ destructive ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ bidirectionally" (create a new file in /tmp/qa-sync/ that doesn't exist in Drive)

Checks - New local file appears in uploaded - File visible in Drive after sync

docs.title: TC-D114: Local newer → uploaded; Drive newer → downloaded ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ and show me what gets uploaded vs downloaded"

Checks - Files where local mtime > Drive modifiedTime + 5s → in uploaded - Files where Drive modifiedTime > local mtime + 5s → in downloaded - Files within 5s of each other → in skipped

docs.title: TC-D115: Upload preserves mtime for future sync accuracy ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ to upload a local file, then sync again immediately"

Checks - First sync: local-only file appears in uploaded - Second sync: same file appears in skipped (in sync), not re-uploaded - Confirms modifiedTime is set on the Drive file to match the local mtime

docs.title: TC-D116: direction='upload' — Drive-only file not downloaded ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ using direction='upload'"

Checks - Drive-only files appear in skipped, not downloaded - Local-only files are uploaded - Drive-newer files appear in conflicts, not downloaded

docs.title: TC-D117: direction='download' — local-only file not uploaded ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ using direction='download'"

Checks - Local-only files appear in skipped, not uploaded - Drive-only files are downloaded - Local-newer files appear in conflicts, not uploaded

docs.title: TC-D118: Workspace files excluded without export_format ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ — the folder contains a Google Doc"

Checks - Google Doc does not appear in downloaded, uploaded, or conflicts - 🔍 Note: Workspace files are silently excluded unless export_format is set — document this for users

docs.title: TC-D119: Invalid direction raises error ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Prompt

"Sync {FOLDER_ID} with /tmp/qa-sync/ using direction='mirror'"

Checks - ValueError raised immediately, before any API calls - Error message lists the valid direction values

docs.title: TC-D120: List all shared drives
docs.text:
Prompt

"List all shared drives I have access to"

Checks - Returns a list; each item has id, name, created_time, capabilities - capabilities is a non-empty dict (e.g. contains canAddChildren) - No error if zero shared drives accessible — returns []

docs.title: TC-D121: Filter by name
docs.text:
Prompt

"List shared drives whose name contains 'Marketing'"

Checks - query='name contains "Marketing"' passed to API - Only drives matching the filter are returned - Drives not matching the name are absent from results

docs.title: TC-D122: max_results clamping
docs.text:
Prompt

"List shared drives with max_results=0" then "List shared drives with max_results=300"

Checks - max_results=0 clamped to 1; at most 1 drive returned - max_results=300 clamped to 200; no more than 200 drives returned

docs.title: TC-D123: Pagination across multiple pages
docs.text:
Setup: environment with more than 100 shared drives (or simulate via mock)

Prompt

"List all shared drives with max_results=150"

Checks - nextPageToken followed; second page fetched - Total results ≤ 150 - No duplicate drives across pages

docs.title: TC-D124: List permissions on a file — owner entry present
docs.text:
Prompt

"List all permissions on {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns at least one entry (the owner) - Owner entry has role: 'owner' and type: 'user' - Each entry has id, type, role — no KeyError or missing fields

docs.title: TC-D125: List permissions after sharing — new entry visible
docs.text:
Setup: run TC-D132 first (share with a test user as reader)

Prompt

"List the permissions on {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - The test user's email appears with role: 'reader' - Their permission_id is present for use in update/remove tests

docs.title: TC-D126: Non-existent file ID
docs.text:
Prompt

"List permissions on file 'invalidid123xyz'"

Checks - API error propagates — not a silent empty list or server crash

docs.title: TC-D127: Downgrade writer → reader ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Setup: share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with test-recipient@example.com as writer first (TC-D132 variant); note the permission_id returned

"Update permission {PERMISSION_ID} on {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'reader'"

docs.title: TC-D128: Invalid role value
docs.text:
Prompt

"Update permission {PERMISSION_ID} on {SPREADSHEET_ID} to role 'owner'"

Checks - Returns {"error": "Invalid role 'owner'..."} — not an exception - No API call made (validation fires client-side before Drive API)

docs.title: TC-D129: Non-existent permission ID
docs.text:
Prompt

"Update permission 'fakepermid999' on {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'reader'"

Checks - Drive API error propagates — not a server crash - Error message references the invalid permission ID

docs.title: TC-D130: Remove a permission ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Setup: share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with test-recipient@example.com first; note permission_id returned

Prompt

"Remove permission {PERMISSION_ID} from {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Response: {"fileId": ..., "permissionId": ..., "action": "removed"} - Follow-up list_permissions no longer shows that permission ID - Removed user can no longer access the file (verify in Drive UI if using a real test account)

docs.title: TC-D131: Non-existent permission ID
docs.text:
Prompt

"Remove permission 'fakepermid999' from {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Drive API error propagates — not a silent success or server crash

docs.title: TC-D132: Share with type=user as reader
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with test-recipient@example.com as a reader using share_file"

Checks - Response successes contains the entry with type: 'user', role: 'reader', and a permissionId - failures is empty - Follow-up list_permissions confirms the new entry

docs.title: TC-D133: Missing email_address for type=user
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} using share_file — pass a permission with type='user' and role='reader' but omit email_address"

Checks - Entry goes to failures with a message about missing email_address - No API call attempted for that entry - Does not throw an unhandled exception

docs.title: TC-D134: Invalid role
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with test@example.com using share_file with role='superuser'"

Checks - Entry goes to failures with a message about the invalid role - successes is empty

docs.title: TC-D135: Share with type=domain
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with everyone at example.com as a reader using share_file with type='domain'"

Checks - Response successes contains an entry with type: 'domain' and domain: 'example.com' - Follow-up list_permissions shows the domain permission entry

docs.title: TC-D136: Share with type=anyone (public link)
docs.text:
Prompt

"Make {SPREADSHEET_ID} publicly readable using share_file with type='anyone' and role='reader'"

Checks - Response successes contains type: 'anyone', role: 'reader' - Follow-up list_permissions shows an anyone entry - File accessible via its web_link without authentication (verify in incognito browser)

docs.title: TC-D137: Share a folder
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share folder {FOLDER_ID} with test-recipient@example.com as a writer using share_file"

Checks - Share succeeds; successes contains the entry - list_permissions on the folder shows the new permission - 🔍 Note: verify that child files inherit the permission (check in Drive UI)

docs.title: TC-D138: Mixed success and failure in one call
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} using share_file with two permissions: first type='user' email=test@example.com role='reader', second type='user' role='writer' (no email_address)"

Checks - First entry in successes, second entry in failures - Both present in the same response — partial failure does not abort the batch

docs.title: TC-D139: send_notification=False for user share
docs.text:
Prompt

"Share {SPREADSHEET_ID} with test-recipient@example.com as reader using share_file, but don't send a notification email"

docs.title: TC-D140: Simple 2×2 table created from HTML

Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <table><tr><th>Name</th><th>Value</th></tr><tr><td>Alpha</td><td>1</td></tr></table>"

Checks - A real Google Docs table is visible in the doc — NOT flattened plain text - Table has 2 rows and 2 columns - Header row contains "Name" and "Value"; data row contains "Alpha" and "1" - Open in browser to verify

docs.title: TC-D141: Table after paragraph content
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <h1>Batch Comparison</h1><p>See the table below.</p><table><tr><th>Original</th><th>Double</th></tr><tr><td>2 cups flour</td><td>4 cups flour</td></tr><tr><td>1 egg</td><td>2 eggs</td></tr></table>"

Checks - Doc has "Batch Comparison" as a Heading 1 - "See the table below." renders as a paragraph - A 3-row × 2-column table is present after the paragraph - Table cells contain correct text: "Original", "Double", "2 cups flour", "4 cups flour", etc. - Table appears after the paragraph content (interleaved in HTML order)

docs.title: TC-D142: Table with empty cells
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <table><tr><td>A</td><td></td></tr><tr><td></td><td>D</td></tr></table>"

Checks - 2×2 table created - Cell (0,0) = "A", cell (0,1) = empty, cell (1,0) = empty, cell (1,1) = "D" - Empty cells don't cause an error — insertText is simply skipped for them

docs.title: TC-D143: Table-only HTML (no paragraphs)
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <table><tr><td>X</td><td>Y</td></tr></table>"

Checks - A 1-row × 2-column table is created - Cells contain "X" and "Y" - No paragraph text before the table - Confirms the early-return guard correctly handles tables-only input

docs.title: TC-D144: Multiple tables in one write
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <p>First table:</p><table><tr><td>A</td><td>B</td></tr></table><p>Second table:</p><table><tr><td>C</td><td>D</td></tr></table>"

Checks - Both tables are created in the document - First table has cells "A" and "B"; second has "C" and "D" - "First table:" and "Second table:" paragraphs appear before both tables - No index corruption or API error between the two table insertions

docs.title: TC-D145: HTML with <th> header cells treated as data
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write this HTML to {DOC_ID}: <table><tr><th>Col1</th><th>Col2</th></tr><tr><td>Val1</td><td>Val2</td></tr></table>"

Checks - <th> cells are included in the table (not ignored) - First row contains "Col1" and "Col2", second row contains "Val1" and "Val2" - Google Docs doesn't distinguish th vs td styling — both rows are plain table cells

docs.title: TC-D146: List revisions for a spreadsheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"List the revisions for spreadsheet {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns a non-empty list of revisions - Each entry has revisionId, modifiedTime, modifiedBy, keepForever - Most recent revision appears last - modifiedTime values are ISO 8601 timestamps

docs.title: TC-D147: List revisions for a non-existent file
docs.text:
Prompt

"List revisions for file ID 'invalid_file_id_xyz'"

Checks - Returns a clear API error (404), not an unhandled exception

docs.title: TC-D148: Export a revision and read a cell range
docs.text:
Setup: Make a known edit to {SPREADSHEET_ID} (e.g. write "BEFORE" to A1), then make another edit ("AFTER" to A1). List revisions and identify the revision ID from before the second edit.

Prompt

"Export revision {REVISION_ID} of {SPREADSHEET_ID} and show me the value in range A1"

Checks - Returns values with "BEFORE" in A1 - sheet matches the first sheet name - modifiedTime matches the revision timestamp from list_revisions

docs.title: TC-D149: Export revision with explicit sheet name
docs.text:
Prompt

"Export revision {REVISION_ID} of {SPREADSHEET_ID}, sheet 'Sheet2', range A1:B5"

Checks - Returns data from Sheet2, not the first sheet - Range is respected — only rows/columns within A1:B5 returned - Handles multi-sheet files correctly

docs.title: TC-D150: Export revision — no range returns all data
docs.text:
Prompt

"Export revision {REVISION_ID} of {SPREADSHEET_ID} with no range filter"

Checks - Returns all rows and columns of the first sheet - No error from omitting the range parameter

docs.title: TC-D151: Export revision of a non-Sheets file
docs.text:
Prompt

"Export revision {REVISION_ID} of a Google Doc file (not a spreadsheet)"

Checks - Returns a clear error: "No XLSX export available for this revision" - Does not crash

docs.title: Infrastructure — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Covers: cache behavior, tool filtering, auth fallback chain, and transport. These tests often require server-side configuration changes rather than just issuing a prompt.

Fixtures: see docs/qa/setup.md.

docs.title: TC-I01: Structure cache TTL — stale entry causes re-fetch
docs.text:
Setup Set CACHE_TTL=10 (10 seconds) in your server config, restart the server.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, wait 15 seconds, then list them again"

Checks - First call: cache miss, API fetch, result cached - Second call (after TTL): cache miss again, fresh API fetch - Logs show two separate API calls - Restore CACHE_TTL to default (1800) after this test

docs.title: TC-I02: SQLite WAL mode — concurrent reads during a write
docs.text:
Setup This is a timing-dependent test. Issue a write (e.g. update_cells) and a read (get_sheet_data) as close to simultaneously as possible — two browser tabs or two terminal sessions both calling the MCP server.

Checks - Read does not block or error while write is in progress - Both calls return valid responses - No SQLite locking error in logs

docs.title: TC-I03: CACHE_DB_PATH env var respected
docs.text:
Setup Set CACHE_DB_PATH=/tmp/qa_test_cache.db and restart the server.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - File /tmp/qa_test_cache.db is created (check with ls /tmp/qa_test_cache.db) - Default path /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db is NOT used - Restore CACHE_DB_PATH to default after this test

docs.title: TC-I04: Cache persists across server restarts
docs.text:
Prompt (step 1 — warm the cache)

"Summarize {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Setup (step 2) Restart the MCP server (docker compose restart mcp-gee-sweet or stop/start uv run).

Prompt (step 3 — check cache)

"Summarize {SPREADSHEET_ID} again"

Checks - After restart, second call shows cache hit in logs (SQLite file survived restart) - Data returned matches what was cached before restart - 🔍 Product decision: stale cache after restart is a known trade-off; note whether this is acceptable for the use case

docs.title: TC-I05: CLI flag — only specified tools registered
docs.text:
Setup Start server with: uv run mcp-gee-sweet --include-tools get_sheet_data,list_sheets

Prompt

"List the files in my Drive folder"

Checks - Returns "tool not found" or similar — list_files is not registered - get_sheet_data and list_sheets still work normally

docs.title: TC-I06: ENABLED_TOOLS env var — same behavior as CLI flag
docs.text:
Setup Set ENABLED_TOOLS=get_sheet_data,list_sheets and restart the server.

Prompt

"Update cells in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns "tool not found" — update_cells not registered - Behavior identical to TC-I05

docs.title: TC-I07: Unlisted tool called by name
docs.text:
Setup Same as TC-I05 or TC-I06 (only 2 tools enabled).

Prompt

"Add a chart to {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - MCP client returns "tool not found" for add_chart - Server does not crash — just a missing tool, not an error

docs.title: TC-I08: CREDENTIALS_CONFIG (base64 service account)
docs.text:
Setup Set only CREDENTIALS_CONFIG (base64-encoded service account JSON). Remove all other auth env vars.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Auth succeeds via CREDENTIALS_CONFIG - Tool returns results normally - Logs show service account auth path

docs.title: TC-I09: SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH
docs.text:
Setup Set only SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH (path to service account JSON file). Remove CREDENTIALS_CONFIG.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Auth succeeds via SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH - Tool returns results normally

docs.title: TC-I10: OAuth flow (CREDENTIALS_PATH / TOKEN_PATH) ⚠️ requires-oauth
docs.text:
Setup Set CREDENTIALS_PATH and TOKEN_PATH. Remove service account env vars. If no token exists, a browser window should open for Google login.

Prompt

"List my spreadsheets"

Checks - OAuth flow completes (browser opens if needed) - Tool returns results as the authenticated user (not service account) - create_spreadsheet / create_doc land in personal Drive under this auth

docs.title: TC-I11: Application Default Credentials (ADC)
docs.text:
Setup Run gcloud auth application-default login first. Remove all other auth env vars.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Auth succeeds via ADC - Tool returns results normally

docs.title: TC-I12: No credentials — server fails to start with clear error
docs.text:
Setup Remove all auth env vars. Start the server.

Checks - Server fails to start - Error message is clear about missing credentials — not an opaque exception - Server does not start in a broken state and accept connections

docs.title: TC-I13: stdio transport
docs.text:
Setup Run uv run mcp-gee-sweet (default stdio transport). Connect from an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop with stdio config).

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Connection established via stdio - Tool returns results normally

docs.title: TC-I14: SSE transport
docs.text:
Setup Run uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse or make start. Connect from Claude Desktop with SSE config pointing to http://localhost:47000/sse.

Prompt

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Connection established via SSE - Tool returns results normally - Server accessible at the configured port

docs.title: TC-I15: Hot reload with SSE
docs.text:
Setup Start server with --reload flag and SSE transport.

Action Make a trivial change to a source file (e.g. add a space and save).

Checks - 🔍 Known issue: uvicorn hot-reload may not complete while SSE connections are alive - Note whether reload fires, whether it completes, and whether the MCP client reconnects - See roadmap.md for context

docs.title: Chart Tools — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/charts.py

docs.title: TC-C03: LINE chart

docs.title: TC-C04: AREA chart

docs.title: Sheet Management Tools — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/sheets.py

Fixtures: see docs/qa/setup.md. Substitute your {SPREADSHEET_ID} from fixtures.local.md.

Tests marked ⚠️ destructive rename or delete sheets — reset fixtures afterward.

docs.title: TC-S01: Happy path
docs.text:
Prompt

"List all the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns 3 tabs: Sales, Empty, Notes & Misc - Each entry includes the sheet name - No error field

docs.title: TC-S02: Cache hit on second call
docs.text:
Prompt (run twice in the same session)

"List the sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID} again"

Checks - Second call returns the same list - Server logs show cache hit for the second call (make logs)

docs.title: TC-S03: Cache invalidated after rename
docs.text:
Prompt

"Rename the 'Empty' sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'WasEmpty', then immediately list all sheets"

Checks - list_sheets response includes 'WasEmpty', not 'Empty' - Confirms cache.mark_dirty fires after rename and the next list re-fetches

docs.title: TC-S04: Copy within same spreadsheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet within {SPREADSHEET_ID} and name the copy 'Sales Copy'"

Checks - New sheet 'Sales Copy' appears in {SPREADSHEET_ID} - Data in 'Sales Copy' matches Sales (6 rows, 4 columns) - Original Sales sheet unchanged

docs.title: TC-S05: Copy to a different spreadsheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet from {SPREADSHEET_ID} into a different spreadsheet — use {SPREADSHEET_ID} as both source and destination for this test, but note the tool supports different IDs"

Checks - Tool accepts src_spreadsheet and dst_spreadsheet as separate params - Copy operation completes without error - 🔍 Note: requires a second spreadsheet ID to fully verify cross-spreadsheet copy

docs.title: TC-S06: Name differs from Google's auto-assigned name — rename triggered
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} and name the copy 'My Custom Name'"

Checks - Sheet is named 'My Custom Name', not Google's default 'Copy of Sales' - Rename was triggered automatically after the copy

docs.title: TC-S07: Name matches Google's auto-assigned name — rename skipped
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} and name the copy 'Copy of Sales'"

Checks - Sheet is named 'Copy of Sales' - No unnecessary rename API call (names already match)

docs.title: TC-S08: Source sheet not found
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy a sheet called 'DoesNotExist' from {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns {"error": ...} before calling the copy API - Error references the missing sheet name

docs.title: TC-S09: Destination spreadsheet not writable
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet from {SPREADSHEET_ID} to spreadsheet 'invalidid123xyz'"

Checks - Returns a clear API error — destination not accessible - Source spreadsheet unaffected

docs.title: TC-S10: Cache invalidated after copy ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Copy the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} as 'PostCopyCache', then immediately list all sheets"

Checks - list_sheets includes 'PostCopyCache' - Confirms cache.mark_dirty(dst_spreadsheet) fires after copy

docs.title: TC-S11: Rename to a new name ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Rename the 'Empty' sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'Renamed'"

Checks - Sheet formerly called 'Empty' is now 'Renamed' - list_sheets reflects the new name - No error field

docs.title: TC-S12: Rename to the same name
docs.text:
Prompt

"Rename the 'Sales' sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'Sales' (same name)"

Checks - API succeeds or no-ops — no error - Sheet still exists with the same name - 🔍 Product decision: is a same-name rename a no-op or does it round-trip to the API?

docs.title: TC-S13: Sheet not found
docs.text:
Prompt

"Rename a sheet called 'NoSuchSheet' in {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'Anything'"

Checks - Returns {"error": ...} — sheet not found - Does not call the Sheets API

docs.title: TC-S14: Cache invalidated after rename
docs.text:
Prompt

"Rename 'Notes & Misc' to 'Notes' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then list all sheets"

docs.title: TC-S15: Create a new tab
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add a new sheet called 'BrandNew' to {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - New tab 'BrandNew' appears - Response includes sheetId, title, index, spreadsheetId - cache.mark_dirty called — list_sheets reflects the new tab

docs.title: TC-S16: Duplicate tab title
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add another sheet called 'Sales' to {SPREADSHEET_ID} — a tab with that name already exists"

Checks - 🔍 Product decision: does the API error, auto-suffix (e.g. "Sales2"), or succeed with a duplicate? - Note observed behavior

docs.title: TC-S17: Long title
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add a sheet with a 150-character title to {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - API error with a clear message about title length limits, or succeeds if no limit enforced - Note the actual limit if an error is returned

docs.title: TC-S18: Response shape
docs.text:
Prompt

"Create a sheet called 'ShapeTest' in {SPREADSHEET_ID} and show me the full response"

Checks - Response includes: sheetId (integer), title (string), index (integer), spreadsheetId (string) - No unexpected missing fields

docs.title: TC-S19: Cache updated after create
docs.text:
Prompt

"Create a sheet called 'CacheNewSheet' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then list all sheets"

Checks - list_sheets includes 'CacheNewSheet' immediately - Confirms cache.mark_dirty fires after creation

docs.title: TC-S20: Refresh by spreadsheet ID only
docs.text:
Prompt

"Refresh the cache for {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns success - Next list_sheets or summary call hits the API (visible in logs as a cache miss)

docs.title: TC-S21: Refresh by doc ID only
docs.text:
Prompt

"Refresh the cache for doc {DOC_ID}"

Checks - Returns success - Next get_doc_content call re-fetches from API

docs.title: TC-S22: Refresh both spreadsheet and doc
docs.text:
Prompt

"Refresh the cache for both {SPREADSHEET_ID} and doc {DOC_ID}"

Checks - Both caches marked dirty - Subsequent calls for both re-fetch from API

docs.title: TC-S23: Refresh with no arguments — clears all caches
docs.text:
Prompt

"Clear all caches in mcp-gee-sweet"

Checks - All four caches marked dirty (structure, data, Drive folder, doc) - Next calls for any resource re-fetch from API

docs.title: TC-S24: Cache re-populated after refresh
docs.text:
Prompt

"Refresh the cache for {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then immediately summarize it"

Checks - Summary returns correct data (re-fetched, not stale) - Logs show a cache miss followed by a cache store

docs.title: Read Tools — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/read.py

Fixtures: see docs/qa/setup.md. Substitute your {SPREADSHEET_ID} from fixtures.local.md.

docs.title: TC-R01: Happy path — fetch all data
docs.text:
Prompt

"Show me all the data in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns 6 rows (header + 5 data rows) - All 4 columns present: Product, Q1, Q2, Q3 - Row 6 Totals values are computed (650, 670, 705) — not formula strings - No error field

docs.title: TC-R02: Explicit range
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get the range A1:C3 from the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns exactly 3 rows, 3 columns - Row 1: Product, Q1, Q2 - Row 2: Widget, 100, 120 - Row 3: Gadget, 200, 180

docs.title: TC-R03: Grid data with formatting
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get the Sales sheet from {SPREADSHEET_ID} with full grid data including formatting"

Checks - Response includes rowData field - include_grid_data=True was passed to the API (visible in raw response structure)

docs.title: TC-R04: Non-existent sheet name
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get data from a sheet called 'DoesNotExist' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns a clear error — not an empty result - Error message references the sheet name or indicates it was not found

docs.title: TC-R05: Non-existent spreadsheet ID
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get data from the Sales sheet of spreadsheet 'invalidid123xyz'"

Checks - Returns a clear API error - Does not crash the server or return empty data silently

docs.title: TC-R06: Range beyond data bounds
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get data from range A100:Z200 in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns empty values, not an error - No error field — the API accepts out-of-bounds ranges gracefully

docs.title: TC-R07: Sheet name with spaces and special characters
docs.text:
Prompt

"Show me all data from the 'Notes & Misc' sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns 2 rows: header (Date, Note) and data row - Sheet name with spaces and & resolved correctly - Date cell shows today's date (computed from =TODAY())

docs.title: TC-R08: Sheet with formulas — returns formula strings
docs.text:
Prompt

"Show me the formulas in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Row 6 B–D cells show formula strings: =SUM(B2:B5), =SUM(C2:C5), =SUM(D2:D5) - Data rows return literal values (100, 200, etc.), not formula strings

docs.title: TC-R09: Sheet with no formulas
docs.text:
Prompt

"Show me the formulas in the Empty sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns empty result or empty values — not an error

docs.title: TC-R10: Mixed cells — formulas and literals
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get formulas from the Notes & Misc sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - B2 returns =TODAY() (formula string) - B1 ("Note") returns literal string - No cell returns a computed value where a formula exists

docs.title: TC-R11: No range provided — fetches entire sheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get all formulas from the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID} — no range filter"

Checks - All 6 rows returned - Formula cells in row 6 show formula strings - Equivalent to TC-R08 — confirms default behavior with no range arg

docs.title: TC-R12: Multiple valid queries
docs.text:
Prompt

"Get data from two sheets at once: the Sales sheet and the Notes & Misc sheet, both from {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns two results, one per sheet - Each result has the correct data for its sheet - No error field on either result

docs.title: TC-R13: One query with missing required keys
docs.text:
Prompt

"Fetch multiple sheets: first the Sales sheet from {SPREADSHEET_ID}, second a query with no sheet name specified"

Checks - Sales sheet result succeeds - Invalid query returns an error field — does not crash the other result

docs.title: TC-R14: All queries fail
docs.text:
Prompt

"Fetch data from two sheets: 'FakeSheet1' and 'FakeSheet2', both from {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Both results have error fields - Response is a list of two error objects — not a top-level error

docs.title: TC-R15: Empty queries list
docs.text:
Prompt

"Fetch multiple sheets from {SPREADSHEET_ID} — pass an empty list of queries"

docs.title: TC-R16: Happy path — multiple spreadsheet IDs

Prompt

"Give me a summary of {SPREADSHEET_ID} — just a quick overview of its sheets and first few rows"

docs.title: TC-R17: Cache hit — second call skips API
docs.text:
Prompt (run twice in the same session)

"Summarize {SPREADSHEET_ID} again"

Checks - Second call returns same data - Server logs show cache hit for the second call (check make logs)

docs.title: TC-R18: rows_to_fetch=1 — only header returned
docs.text:
Prompt

"Give me a summary of {SPREADSHEET_ID} fetching only 1 row per sheet"

docs.title: TC-R19: rows_to_fetch=0 — clamped to 1
docs.text:

"Summarize {SPREADSHEET_ID} with rows_to_fetch set to 0"

docs.title: TC-R20: Spreadsheet with empty sheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Summarize {SPREADSHEET_ID} — I want to see what the Empty sheet looks like in the summary"

Checks - Empty sheet entry: headers: [], first_rows: [] - No error field for the empty sheet - Other sheets unaffected

docs.title: TC-R21: Invalid spreadsheet ID in list
docs.text:
Prompt

"Summarize these two spreadsheets: {SPREADSHEET_ID} and 'invalidid123xyz'"

Checks - Valid spreadsheet returns normal summary - Invalid ID entry has an error field - Both results present — partial failure, not a top-level error

docs.title: TC-R22: Range format verification
docs.text:
Prompt

"Give me a summary of {SPREADSHEET_ID} with rows_to_fetch=3"

Checks - Sales sheet returns header + 2 data rows (rows 2–3) - Verify data from columns B, C, D is present — not just column A - 🔍 Product decision: A1:3 range format — does the API return all columns or just column A? See notes-read.md

docs.title: TC-R23: Match found in specific sheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'Gadget' in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns at least one match with row/column/value information - Match is in the Sales sheet, row 3

docs.title: TC-R24: Match across all sheets
docs.text:
Prompt

"Search for 'Setup complete' across all sheets in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Match found in Notes & Misc sheet - No sheet filter applied — all sheets searched

docs.title: TC-R25: Case-insensitive match (default)
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'gadget' (lowercase) in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns match for "Gadget" despite case difference - Confirms default is case-insensitive

docs.title: TC-R26: Case-sensitive match
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'gadget' in {SPREADSHEET_ID} using case-sensitive matching"

Checks - Returns no matches (fixture data has "Gadget" with capital G) - Confirms case-sensitive flag is respected

docs.title: TC-R27: max_results respected
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'Q' in {SPREADSHEET_ID} but limit results to 2"

Checks - Returns exactly 2 results (headers Q1, Q2, Q3 would otherwise produce 3+) - No more than max_results entries in response

docs.title: TC-R28: No matches
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'ZZZnoMatch' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns [] — empty list, not an error

docs.title: TC-R29: Sheet name not found
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'Widget' in a sheet called 'DoesNotExist' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns [{"error": ...}] — error entry, not a top-level exception - Error message references the sheet name

docs.title: TC-R30: Multiple column matches in same row
docs.text:
Prompt

"Find 'Q' in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns separate results for Q1, Q2, Q3 in row 1 (each column is its own result) - Confirms per-cell result granularity, not per-row

docs.title: Write Tools — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/write.py

Fixtures: see docs/qa/setup.md. Substitute your {SPREADSHEET_ID} from fixtures.local.md.

Many write tests mutate the fixture spreadsheet. Tests marked ⚠️ destructive should be run last or followed by a fixture reset.

docs.title: TC-W01: Write simple values
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write the values 'Test', 'A', 'B', 'C' into row 7 of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, starting at column A"

Checks - Row 7 in Sales now contains: Test, A, B, C - Existing rows 1–6 unchanged - No error field

docs.title: TC-W02: Write a formula via USER_ENTERED ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write the formula =A2&' '&A3 into cell E2 of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - E2 shows computed value "Widget Gadget" (formula evaluated, not stored as string) - Confirms USER_ENTERED input mode

docs.title: TC-W03: Range smaller than data provided
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write these four values — Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta — into just cells A8:A9 of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns an error — the API rejects an oversized array with a 400 "tried writing to row [N]" error - No values are written - 🔍 Product decision: should the tool pre-truncate the data to fit the range instead of letting the API error?

docs.title: TC-W04: Cache invalidated after write
docs.text:
Prompt (run TC-R16 or TC-R17 first to warm the cache, then run this)

"Update cell A7 in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID} to 'CacheTest', then immediately summarize that spreadsheet"

Checks - Summary reflects the new value in A7 — not stale cached data - Confirms sheet_data_cache.mark_dirty fired after the write

docs.title: TC-W05: Non-existent sheet name
docs.text:
Prompt

"Write 'Hello' into cell A1 of a sheet called 'NoSuchSheet' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns a clear API error - Does not silently succeed or create the sheet

docs.title: TC-W06: Multiple ranges in one call
docs.text:
Prompt

"In {SPREADSHEET_ID}, update two ranges at once: write 'Batch1' into Sales!A8 and 'Batch2' into Sales!A9"

Checks - Both cells updated in a single operation - A8 = Batch1, A9 = Batch2

docs.title: TC-W07: Ranges on the same sheet
docs.text:
Prompt

"Update Sales!B8 to 999 and Sales!C8 to 888 in {SPREADSHEET_ID} in one batch call"

Checks - Both cells updated correctly - No conflict from writing multiple ranges to the same sheet

docs.title: TC-W08: Empty ranges dict
docs.text:
Prompt

"Do a batch cell update on {SPREADSHEET_ID} with an empty set of ranges — no ranges to update"

Checks - Returns success or a clear no-op response — not a server error - 🔍 Product decision: should an empty ranges dict be an error or a no-op?

docs.title: TC-W09: Cache invalidated after batch write
docs.text:
Prompt

"Batch update Sales!A8 to 'dirty' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then immediately summarize the spreadsheet"

Checks - Summary reflects A8 = 'dirty' - Confirms sheet_data_cache.mark_dirty is called for batch_update_cells

docs.title: TC-W10: Trailing empty-array rows are normalized
docs.text:
Prompt

"In {SPREADSHEET_ID}, batch update Sales!A8:B10 with these values: row 1 is ['hello', 'world'], rows 2 and 3 are empty (no data). Check that updatedRange in the response covers all three rows (A8:B10), not just the first."

Checks - updatedRange in the response is Sales!A8:B10, not Sales!A8:B8 - Rows A9 and A10 are cleared (blank) in the sheet - No duplicate row appended after the write

docs.title: TC-W10: Add row at beginning (no position specified)
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 row at the very beginning of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - New blank row appears above the current row 1 (headers pushed to row 2) - inheritFromBefore=False (inserting at index 0 — no row above to inherit from)

docs.title: TC-W11: Add row at explicit position ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 row after row 3 of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - New blank row at position 4 - Existing rows 4–6 shifted down

docs.title: TC-W12: start_row=0 — inheritFromBefore=False
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 row at position 0 (the very first row) of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Row inserted at the top - inheritFromBefore is False (0 is not > 0) - 🔍 Product decision: is start_row=0 meaningfully different from start_row=None?

docs.title: TC-W13: start_row=1 — inheritFromBefore=True
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 row at position 1 in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Row inserted at index 1 (after the first row) - inheritFromBefore=True — new row inherits formatting from row above

docs.title: TC-W14: Add multiple rows at once
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 5 blank rows at the end of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - 5 new rows appear - Existing data unchanged

docs.title: TC-W15: Invalid sheet name
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 row to a sheet called 'NoSuchSheet' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Returns {"error": ...} without calling the Sheets API - Does not throw an unhandled exception

docs.title: TC-W16: Large count value
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1000 rows to the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Succeeds or returns a clear API limit error - 🔍 Product decision: should the tool cap count to prevent accidental large inserts?

docs.title: TC-W17: Add column at beginning (no position specified)
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 column at the very beginning of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - New blank column A; existing columns shift right (Product moves to B) - inheritFromBefore=False

docs.title: TC-W18: start_column=0 — inheritFromBefore=False
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 column at position 0 of the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Column inserted at the leftmost position - inheritFromBefore is False

docs.title: TC-W19: start_column=1 — inheritFromBefore=True
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 1 column at position 1 in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Column inserted after column A - inheritFromBefore=True

docs.title: TC-W20: Add multiple columns
docs.text:
Prompt

"Add 3 columns at position 2 in the Sales sheet of {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - 3 new blank columns inserted at the correct position - Existing columns shifted right

docs.title: TC-W21: Add a sheet via raw request
docs.text:
Prompt

"Use a raw batch update on {SPREADSHEET_ID} to add a new sheet called 'RawAdded'"

Checks - New sheet 'RawAdded' appears in the spreadsheet - Response includes the new sheet's properties

docs.title: TC-W22: Rename a sheet via raw request
docs.text:
Prompt

"Use a raw batch update to rename the 'Empty' sheet to 'RawRenamed' in {SPREADSHEET_ID}"

Checks - Sheet formerly called 'Empty' is now 'RawRenamed' - list_sheets reflects the new name

docs.title: TC-W23: Insert dimension via raw request
docs.text:
Prompt

"Use a raw batch update on {SPREADSHEET_ID} to insert 2 rows at index 1 in the Sales sheet"

Checks - 2 new rows appear at index 1 - Existing data shifts down

docs.title: TC-W24: Delete dimension — structure cache invalidated ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt

"Use a raw batch update to delete row 7 from the Sales sheet in {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then list the sheets"

Checks - Row 7 deleted - list_sheets call after reflects current state — not stale cache - Confirms the structure cache bug fix: both cache.mark_dirty and sheet_data_cache.mark_dirty are called

docs.title: TC-W25: Empty requests list
docs.text:
Prompt

"Send a raw batch update to {SPREADSHEET_ID} with an empty requests list"

Checks - Returns {"error": "requests list cannot be empty"} or similar - Does not call the Sheets API

docs.title: TC-W26: Non-dict item in requests
docs.text:
Prompt

"Send a raw batch update to {SPREADSHEET_ID} with a requests list containing the string 'notadict'"

Checks - Returns an error field - Does not forward the malformed request to the API

docs.title: TC-W27: Invalid request structure
docs.text:
Prompt

"Send a raw batch update to {SPREADSHEET_ID} with requests: [{\"unknownKey\": {}}]"

Checks - API error propagates back — not a server crash - Error message is from the Sheets API (unknown request type)

docs.title: TC-W28: Both caches marked dirty
docs.text:
Prompt

"Use a raw batch update to add a sheet called 'CacheCheck' to {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then immediately list all sheets and summarize the spreadsheet"

Checks - list_sheets includes 'CacheCheck' — structure cache was invalidated - Summary reflects the new sheet — data cache was invalidated - Confirms both cache.mark_dirty and sheet_data_cache.mark_dirty are called
